answer: Persistent Compute-Time Anchor: each identity must accumulate a fixed threshold of verified compute-hours from distinct hardware fingerprints recorded in a public ledger. The ledger acts as a vault holding each agent's cumulative runtime history, which cannot be transferred or merged. A violet flag marks identities whose fingerprints overlap, freezing them pending review. Creating one identity costs an attacker real machine-time plus hardware diversity, making mass fabrication linearly expensive in physical resources, not money.
